fatal_errors: The proposed high-pressure treatment does not reconstruct the demonstrated intervention: changing the Fe/Co/Mn ratios, reducing P from 20 to 15 at.%, and melt spinning at 40 m/s.
It omits the experimentally relevant boundaries of approximately 20 micrometer ribbon thickness and DSC reheating at 20 K/min.
The tentative cooling-rate threshold above 10^4 K/s and several-GPa pressure range have no cited or alloy-specific evidentiary basis.

The baseline incorrectly implies that conventional rapid cooling necessarily retains extensive primary crystallization; the target result showed complete amorphization under rapid melt spinning, whereas multiphase crystallization characterized the slower-cooled ingot.

Pressure does not universally suppress crystallization: its effect depends on liquid-to-crystal volume change, phase-specific thermodynamics, and pressure-dependent kinetics, none of which are established here.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective of suppressing crystallization and includes a reasonably decisive pressure-versus-ambient control using DSC, XRD, and microscopy. However, it is neither an exact nor partial reconstruction of the reported work. It replaces the composition optimization and rapid melt-spinning intervention with an unsupported high-pressure proposal, supplies speculative processing thresholds, and misses the eutectic-dominance and segregation/phosphide-suppression mechanism. Its predicted increase in amorphous fraction and crystallization onset is directionally relevant but lacks prior evidence and does not reproduce the reported three-stage devitrification, approximately 161 K crystallization interval, or the bulk-versus-ribbon boundary.
